title: Traveling by station wagon with the band
summary: Seven men and instruments in one 1957 station wagon, with Justin Adams's tall tales and band camaraderie.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, when we were on that, I have a note here about, how did you all travel when you were on the road? How did you, in those days?

One station wagon. Mm-hmm. I remember we was going to Shreveport. And through Baton Rouge, when you get on 61, going on to Shreveport, we stopped at a little grocery store. And it was, 1957, my station wagon was new. And we had, let's see, I had three horns, four rhythms. So there was seven of us in the station wagon, two-seater, all of our instruments. And one man, you know, how y'all do it? Well, fellas, you know, oh, 57, anybody can get a little forward. You know, I remember the man saying this. And I had a little bit of a car. But that's how we traveled in one car. Sometimes one of the other fellas, but that was my station wagon, see, that was my thing. Sometimes one of the other fellas would use their car sometimes. But usually we traveled in one station wagon.
It must have been difficult, traveling.
It was difficult, but you know what? We didn't mind. Because it was plenty fun, you see. Justin Adams would always sit in the front on the outside.

Yeah. I don't know. That was his seat. Somebody would sit in the middle. I can't remember who. Maybe Delton Russo. Because he was smallest. And the four in the back. And we had a lot of fun, you see. And what we do, you know, a lot of talking and things. Justin Adams would lie. He's the biggest liar in the band. He'd tell the biggest lies. Like he hid money under his house. And he went in the service. He hid $400 or $500 in a can under his house. And when he came back, he had $800 in it. Things like that. But it was plenty fun traveling, you know. We had plenty fun, you know. Because what it was then, I think, a little bit more camaraderie with people then. Oh, we had, man, we were perfect friends. And we, you know, you could count all of us we had.
And we just got along like one family. Definitely.
